newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dairy Board cool on oil barter with Iran.
newsitem.headline: NZ Dairy Board cool on oil barter with Iran.

text.p: The New Zealand Dairy Board would look at any proposal to barter dairy products for Iranian oil, but was not enthusiastic about bartering, a board spokesman said on Monday.
He was responding to a reported suggestion by Iranian Ambassador Mohammed Sazgara that a proposed wool-for-oil deal with Iran was dependent on the involvement of the Dairy Board and the Meat Board.

"The ambassador hasn't yet approached us with his proposition and were he to do so, obviously we would look at it as any other. That said, it would be something of a departure for us," Dairy Board spokesman Neville Martin said.
Asked if the board was making any initiative on the matter, Martin said: "No."
The Dominion newspaper quoted Sazgara as saying the deal could be worth NZ$50 million, but that Iran did not want $50 million of wool alone.

Wool Services International chief executive Michael Dwyer confirmed he was negotiating with Iran but said no deal was in place. "There is no deal, unfortunately, but we would like to think there would be one in time," Dwyer said.

Martin said the only barter deal done by the Dairy Board was about 15 years ago when it swapped Iranian light crude for dairy products "with our fingers crossed and chewing our fingernails throughout the exercise, because that is the worry of barter".
He added: "People don't tend to barter things when the market is rising. It was a satisfactory transaction, but not one we are particularly fond of."
He said the board already sold substantial quantities of dairy products to Iran and would only look at a deal that would increase volumes.
"We are in a well sold-up position on all products, notably butter, the Russians having bought fairly heavily this year," Martin said.
A spokesman for Middle East exporter Alliance said meat companies would not encourage barter trade.
